title: KV cache chaos + recovery playbook (hands-on lab)
content:
Purpose and audience
This is a hands-on lab for solutions engineering workshops with customers who want to understand how Redwood's runtime behaves when the KV (key/value) attention cache experiences transient corruption, eviction storms, or network partitions. Audience: SEs running a 2‑3 hour workshop with ML/infra engineers from a customer. The doc is intentionally tactical: scripts, checks, and instructor notes.

Learning objectives
- Observe latency and token-level error patterns when KV cache returns stale/incorrect entries.
- Trigger controlled failure modes (bit-flip simulation, partial eviction, RPC latency spikes).
- Exercise runtime fallback: model variant fallback, cache bypass, and graceful throttle.
- Validate recovery: warmup sequences, cache repopulation, and throughput stabilization.
- Collect traces/metrics and map to SLO implications (p50/p95/p99, token cost).

Prereqs (customer + lab environment)
- Private deployment or dedicated test pool with a single serving group (one or two GPU nodes) running the demo model (Llama-2-7b-like).
- Access to control-plane CLI and SSH to inference nodes.
- Metric pipeline: Prometheus + Grafana dashboard with token/latency/error metrics. Example dashboard JSON linked above.
- Small sample workload generator (included in linked repo).
- Test account with RBAC so attendees can trigger experiments without risking prod.

High-level flow (2–3 hours)
1) Intro (10 min): quick architecture recap: where KV cache sits, what it stores, and how it is used across requests.
2) Baseline (20–30 min): run steady load (50 qps small prompts) and capture baseline metrics.
3) Experiment 1 - partial eviction (20 min): evict cache entries on one pod and see missed cache hits, latency delta, and model tokens regenerated.
4) Experiment 2 - corrupted responses (20 min): return wrong cache entries for a suffix and watch hallucination/regeneration patterns.
5) Experiment 3 - network latency spike (25 min): add 100–300ms latency between adapter and cache backend and measure p99 increase and batching behaviour.
6) Recovery & mitigations (30 min): show automatic fallbacks, manual switch to cache-bypass, and warmup strategies.
7) Wrap-up (15 min): findings, recommended config changes, next steps.

Instructor notes
- Keep safety: do not run heavy experiments on customer production clusters. Prefer Dedicated test pools or staging.
- Bring a second cluster snapshot for rollback.
- Have the model variant fallback pre-configured in the console so you can flip it quickly.
- Emphasize observability: show token-level traces and generated-text diffs to make the impact concrete.

Commands & small scripts (examples)
(1) run baseline generator (in attendee VM)
python3 tools/loadgen.py --endpoint https://inference.test.redwood/api/generate --concurrency 8 --qps 50 --prompt-file samples/prompts-short.txt --duration 600 --save-results out/baseline.json

(2) evict KV entries on node-2 (simulated)
# ssh into node-2 and run eviction helper
ssh ubuntu@node-2 "sudo -u redwood /opt/redwood/bin/kvtool evict --prefix session:demo --rate 2000"
(quick note: the evict command is non-destructive, it simulates eviction by marking entries expired for the runtime)

(3) simulate corruption (in adapter process)
# swap in the chaos filter (preloaded in /opt/chaos/kv_injector.so)
sudo LD_PRELOAD=/opt/chaos/kv_injector.so /opt/redwood/bin/adapter --config /etc/redwood/adapter-chaos.yaml &
# the injector has toggles: flip-rate=0.01 (1% of reads return corrupted bytes), scope=session-id-prefix

(4) add network latency between adapter and cache backend (tc netem)
sudo tc qdisc add dev eth1 root netem delay 200ms 50ms distribution normal
# remove when done
sudo tc qdisc del dev eth1 root netem

Observability checklist (what to watch)
- Cache hit rate (per pod), cache read latencies, and read error rates.
- Token generation deltas: number of tokens generated per request pre/post experiment. Large jumps => regeneration due to missed cache.
- Model output diffs: compare baseline vs experiment outputs (tools/diff-out.py) to show hallucination/regression.
- Traces: span breakdown (adapter -> runtime -> KV -> model) to map where time is spent.
- Billing metrics: token count increases and GPU-util changes.

Expected behaviors and troubleshooting tips
- Partial eviction => immediate drop in cache hit rate on target pod(s), p95 latency rises as runtime falls back to autoregressive generation. Expect token-cost uptick.
- Corrupted cache entries => observed as small content regressions or failed structured outputs (if using tool calls). Recommend fail-fast detection: checksum per cache entry and fallback.
- Network latency spike => batching behavior may improve throughput but hurts tail latency. If p99 > SLO, enable per-request low-latency path in routing policy.
- If you see adapter crashes after injecting LD_PRELOAD chaos, revert and check symbol mismatch. Always keep a stable adapter binary on standby.

Mitigation recipes (demo quick wins)
- Enable read-checksum verification on cache reads (config flag) so runtime validates entry integrity and falls back on mismatch.
- Route a % of traffic to a no-cache path (canary) to validate user-visible quality while rolling configuration. Use console rollout: create canary route with traffic 5%.
- Warmup strategy: after recovery, send warmup sequences (popular prompts) to repopulate the cache. Use tools/warmup-seqs.txt.
- Autoscale policy: configure burst capacity so that node eviction doesn't immediately saturate remaining nodes.

Lab exercises for attendees (short tasks)
- Exercise A: run baseline and compute token delta after a 5-minute eviction. Submit results to the shared sheet.
- Exercise B: flip corruption on 0.5% of reads and find 3 examples where the model output changes structurally (e.g., JSON response changes). Capture diffs.
- Exercise C: use the Console to create a canary route that bypasses KV cache for 10% of traffic; observe metrics and verify quality differences.

Artifacts to hand out (links)
- loadgen tool: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-tools/tree/main/loadgen
- chaos injector binary and source: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-tools/tree/main/kv_injector
- dashboard JSON: linked in linked_artifacts above

Post-workshop recommendations for customers
- Turn on read checksums and a non-zero canary bypass for 1–2 weeks to validate in production.
- Add an alert for cache-hit-rate drop > 20% sustained for 1 minute.
- Create a warmup job run after deployments that touches top-200 prompt patterns to reduce cold-regeneration.

Open issues / TODOs for SE follow-up
- Add a guided script that auto-runs the three chaos experiments and collects a single report. (Evan to prototype).
- Improve the injector to support config via HTTP control plane rather than LD_PRELOAD (Marisol).
- Add example Prometheus recording rules that correlate token-cost with cache-hit-rate (Derrick).

Notes to self (instructor)
- Demo quick rollback: pre-baked IAM role to disable chaos tools and revert adapter.
- Keep slide deck minimal: architecture diagram, expected impact table, and checklist.

End of doc.
